newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rio state, federal gov't to discuss debt deal Fri.
newsitem.headline: Rio state, federal gov't to discuss debt deal Fri.

text.p: Rio de Janeiro state and federal officials will meet this afternoon to discuss final details of a debt restructuring deal expected to be unveiled next week, a spokesman for Rio's Planning office said.

The rescheduling deal for Rio de Janeiro's 11.3 billion real debt hinges on a decision by the federal government not to raise the interest rates it will charge to refinance the major part of the debt, the spokesman said.

Under a government decree on the restructuring of state debts, state governments have to pay off 20 percent of their debts through asset sales. The remainder would be refinanced over 30 years paying annual interest rates of six percent.

The federal government apparently was considering that Rio de Janeiro state's assets were not enough to cover the 20 percent of the debt, which would make the state pay higher rates to have its debt refinanced.

Rio de Janeiro state argues that state bank Banerj, which is expected to be privatized in February, and Banerj's assets under liquidation will provide most of the resources needed to pay off 20 percent of the debt.
The debt agreement with the federal government is key to allow the new bid specifications for Banerj's sell-off to be published, the spokesman said.
The tender document is expected to be published later this month.
Banerj, whose sell-off has been postponed twice due to court rulings, is due to be the first of Brazilian state banks to be privatized.
((--Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom 5511 2485412)) (c) Reuters Limited 1997
